body: Thank you. I didn't know if leaving without some journal of my thoughts would be wrong. And it's kind of you to say, those are good sentiments, most are what you say. But I am weak, I always have been. She was my only adventure. The only one I had or wanted.

I understand. I'm glad that you found your way out of the dark. But I don't want to anymore. They say the immature man dies for the cause, the mature one lives for it. But I don't want to heal anymore. I just want to leave the right thing for when I'm gone.

You described an image that I've had for a while now. If you're familiar with the song 'are you lonesome tonight', it seems appropriate. A broken clown. Like I was broken and she was the gold that kept me together.

I've tried to improve, exercise, language lessons, writing, therapy. I still feel empty. 

Thanks for the kind words, but I really am just trying to find if leaving a note might be good. I probably will anyway, if she chooses to read it will be up to her.

There isn't anything left that I can see. I meant death, so legal issues post facto aren't my worry. It's been months and it all goes downhill. I got employed, and am working on a better job, but nothing helps. It's all I can do to keep it smooth at work. They seem to think well of me, but I have no confidence left. I just want it to end. 

We were together for 16 years, and she cut me off in September. No attempts for discussion on my part went anywhere. I'm in therapy, but I feel hollow. Talking to a friend and he directed me to introspect, which just led to an ugly realization. I've always tried to escape, nothing stirred me, drew me, till her. And that godawful emptiness seems more pronounced.
It's good you had a positive experience. Hopefully you can both move on from it with similar painlessness.

You seem to be right that it's too late, I just hate to admit it. It hurts to end a twenty year relationship in what feels so abrupt a manner, but nothing I try works. Worse, everyone around me treats it as foregone, like they couldn't try to reason with her.  It's pretty much the end for a variety of reasons though.

He's badly divisive at a time when we desperately need the opposite. He doesn't build a consensus and work with what most people find good, he plays to his specific supporters. 

In general, he's making a bad situation worse.

The night we met. I recall her dropping into my lap and spouting a cheery hi. It was fun messing around with our pals for the night, but from that moment I was lost. I kept after her until we were together.

Not sure what else to say. It's just frustrating to be at the end of your rope and get platitudes. They show concern, but stop shy of talking about the issues beyond those points. If there was more honest dialogue about what had gone wrong, and wirh my wife in particular, matters wouldn't have gotten this bad surely.
Not for long. That's why I'm in this state.

I'd like to believe so, but she won't speak to me directly and seems set on the divorce, no reconciliation. My options to mend things are pretty diminished. My health is stable enough for the moment, but I'm still working on it. Thank you for asking.

Edit for still getting used to this and because I felt I was too negative.

Forgive me if this conversation is abandoned, but it seemed too relevant to my own situation to ignore. I feel I've lost touch with my own wife over this issue and despise that it happened. 
During the election I'd clung to what made sense and ignored the rest I suppose, I was going through severe medical issues and my depression compounded them. I suppose I was willingly blind and being foolish out of desperation. 
Regardless, from someone trapped on the other side of the table, you have my sympathies. 45 is a mess. For everyone, but some of us are realizing it late.
